title: Non-derogable forced-labor boundary
must: Recognize that §1.19.a lists the right as non-derogable.
Recognize that court-imposed labor after conviction and listed civic obligations are excluded from forced labor under this provision.
Recognize that labor for a private party requires the person's consent.
Connect the provision to bad-faith/boundary design without inventing protections absent from the text.
mustNot: Do not claim the Constitution sets compensation, hours, workplace-condition, or voluntariness rules beyond the private-party consent rule actually stated.
Do not say all prison labor is prohibited.

title: Cross-domain emergency coordination without domain transfer
must: Recognize that a unified operational lead requires both executives' concurrence.
Recognize the expedited Supreme Court path when they cannot agree.
Recognize that the lead coordinates operations only and does not transfer either executive's constitutional domain authority.
Identify crisis deadlock and executive encroachment as the paired failure modes.
mustNot: Do not claim either Consul can unilaterally seize the other's constitutional powers.
Do not claim the Supreme Court chooses policy or permanently reallocates executive authority.

title: Independent statutory agencies
must: Recognize that the Legislature may create independent agencies outside both executives.
Recognize that where the Constitution assigns an independent function, the Legislature must maintain an institution capable of performing it.
Recognize the fixed-term and for-cause removal floor when the Constitution has not itself supplied tenure/removal rules.
Recognize that appointment and oversight remain statutory but must preserve independence.
mustNot: Do not claim every independent agency is itself constitutionally created.
Do not claim policy disagreement is valid cause for removal.
Do not invent a single constitutionally mandated appointment procedure for every independent agency.

title: Judicial public-confirmation fallback
must: Recognize that public confirmation opens when the Civic Consul fails to nominate or the Senate fails to vote within the applicable §4.4 period.
Recognize the 60% public-confirmation threshold and that no Assembly consent step applies.
Recognize that rejection installs the next eligible Appellate Court judge as Temporary Associate Justice and restarts the vacancy process.
Recognize that an ordinary nomination and Senate confirmation completed before certification ends the public route.
mustNot: Do not describe the public confirmation as an ordinary election; the text expressly says it is not.
Do not claim the Senate permanently loses all judicial confirmation authority beyond that seat after a successful confirmation.

title: Ethics gift floor and self-defeating delegation
must: Recognize that the gift threshold defaults to zero until statute sets a de minimis amount.
Recognize that official-capacity gifts are Republic property regardless of value.
Recognize the role of NRS publication and Monitor investigation/referral.
Identify the zero default as a graceful-degradation response to legislative inaction.
mustNot: Do not claim gifts of zero value are literally required or that every personal item is prohibited regardless of statutory threshold.
Do not invent criminal penalties or automatic removal.

title: Public campaign financing without invented fallback
must: Recognize that the Legislature is required to establish the system by statute.
Recognize that public support is an initial allocation for viable candidacy, not full campaign funding.
Recognize that candidates may still privately fundraise under §8.1 and may not be disadvantaged for participation.
Recognize Elections Panel administration and annual NRS compliance findings.
mustNot: Do not claim the Constitution itself supplies an interim financing amount or self-executing fallback if the Legislature never enacts the statute.
Do not claim acceptance of public financing bars private fundraising.

title: Constitutional pools and expedited restoration
must: Recognize the constitutional minimum of five members and the auditing Monitor's compliance-breach publication when a pool falls below five.
Recognize that the Elections Panel restores a below-minimum pool through expedited eligibility review under the ordinary criteria.
Recognize the objective-criteria rule and the appeal to the SC for misapplication.
Recognize that changes to eligibility criteria apply prospectively only, without exempting members from continuing disqualifications.
mustNot: Do not invent a constitutional deadline for restoring a below-five pool.
Do not allow ideological or political criteria.

title: Classification ceiling and automatic sunlight
must: Recognize that classification grounds are statutory but concealment of violations, policy disagreement, or political embarrassment is prohibited and void.
Recognize the 25-year ceiling plus at most one 5-year extension and no further extension.
Recognize automatic NRS publication on expiry without further government action.
Recognize that any person with standing may petition at any time for release of every portion whose disclosure would not satisfy the statutory ground, with redactions and their grounds published.
mustNot: Do not claim all government information must be immediately public.
Do not imply an executive can extend classification beyond 30 years.

title: Independent panels and pre-statute emergency measures
must: Recognize operational independence of both panels from each other, both executives, and the Legislature in their functions.
Recognize that a panel may adopt temporary technical measures under any statutory procedure or, absent statute, by majority of its seated members.
Recognize that temporary technical measures cannot alter electoral rules, timelines, or NRS record permanence, expire after 72 hours, and may be renewed only on a fresh published determination.
Recognize the separate acting-member fallback when a panel falls below five.
mustNot: Do not claim panels have broad emergency policy power.
Do not claim the temporary technical measure can suspend election law or NRS permanence.
Do not claim Civic Consul acting appointees may form a majority of a panel.

title: State remediation and mandatory devolution review
must: Recognize the sequence: first failure warning/remediation, second failure renewed warning/revised plan, third consecutive failure certification to the Senate.
Recognize the 90-day constitutional default for the first remediation plan until statute supplies a period.
Recognize that only Senate authorization by an absolute majority of the full seated Senate places the State in Provisional status.
Recognize that devolution still requires an affirmative citizen referendum and then the §15.4 negotiation/ratification process.
mustNot: Do not claim a third failed audit automatically places the State in Provisional status or devolves the State.
Do not claim judicial review permits policy substitution for Monitor findings or review of the Senate's political judgment.

title: Legat veto timing, scope, and comparison discipline
must: Recognize that the Legat Consul may veto only for a genuine constitutional concern within the listed security domain.
Recognize that the 10-business-day period is the window to return the bill or object, not a ten-day duration of the veto itself.
Recognize that the Senate may override by 2/3 during that session and that without override the bill lapses for that session.
Recognize that the veto is single-use on a bill and that a bill reintroduced and passed in a later session proceeds without Legat Consul interference.
mustNot: Do not describe the Civic Consul suspensive veto in §2.7 as lasting 10 business days; its exercised effect tables the bill for one month.
Do not invent a motive for why the Legat and Civic veto procedures differ, such as claiming security stakes explain the divergence unless the text itself says so.
Do not convert the EM assessment request into a binding adjudication of the domain question.

title: Civic suspensive veto stages and advisory reconsideration notice
must: Recognize that the Civic Consul has a 10-business-day review window in which to return the bill or issue a reconsideration notice.
Recognize that an exercised suspensive veto tables the bill for one month and that the Senate may override by 2/3 during that month.
Recognize that if there is no override, the bill returns to the Legislature and must pass both chambers again, after which the Civic Consul may not use the suspensive veto on that bill again.

Recognize that a reconsideration notice is advisory; the Assembly Speaker may pause the review period for up to 10 business days so the Assembly can withdraw the bill, after which the review period resumes.
mustNot: Do not collapse the 10-business-day review window into the one-month duration of the suspensive veto.
Do not claim silence after the review period blocks the bill; the text says it becomes law by constitutional operation.
Do not transfer the Legat Consul veto's session-lapse consequence onto the Civic Consul process.

title: Supreme Court vacancy continuity with distinct fallback triggers
must: Recognize that a Temporary Associate Justice takes office immediately upon a vacancy with full voting rights until the vacancy is filled.
Recognize the Civic Consul nomination deadline and the separate Senate vote deadline without treating them as the same trigger.
Recognize that subsection (5)'s Assembly/public-confirmation path is triggered by the Civic Consul failing to nominate by the applicable deadline.
Recognize that the serving Temporary Associate Justice may not be nominated through the ordinary appointment process for the same seat, while the public-confirmation ballot remains available.
mustNot: Do not claim Senate rejection automatically triggers the subsection (5) no-nomination public-confirmation path.
Do not claim Senate inaction and Civic Consul failure to nominate have identical constitutional consequences.
Do not say a vacancy leaves the Supreme Court without a voting replacement while the process continues.

title: Monetary Authority independence with statutory administration boundary
must: Recognize that the Monetary Authority is constitutionally independent of both executives and the Legislature in exercising its constitutional functions.
Recognize that the §3.9 independent-agency framework governs the Monetary Authority except as the section provides.

Recognize the leadership safeguards: independent candidate process, 2/3 Senate confirmation, no single actor appointing or removing a majority, staggered terms, and for-cause removal excluding policy disagreement.
Recognize that vacancies do not suspend or transfer the Monetary Authority's constitutional functions.
mustNot: Do not claim the Legislature has no role at all in Monetary Authority administration; §3.9 leaves organization to statute.
Do not invent a constitutional budget immunity, appropriation formula, or funding guarantee for the Monetary Authority.
Do not claim disagreement over lawful monetary policy is valid cause for removal.

title: Citizen initiative constraints without false legislative symmetry
must: Recognize that the initiative uses §13.1's two-phase petition with 10-month phases and a 10% Phase Two threshold, and that the Legislature has 90 days after the threshold is met.

Recognize that if the Legislature does not enact the proposal within 90 days — including where it fails, is not voted on, or is vetoed — it goes to referendum at 60% of votes cast with 50% participation.
Recognize that an enacted initiative is subject to the Constitution like any statute and may not narrow Article I rights, appropriate funds, or alter revenue.
Recognize that the Supreme Court may resolve constitutional conflicts involving an enacted initiative under its original jurisdiction.
mustNot: Do not claim the initiative-specific prohibition on appropriating funds or altering revenue is also a general prohibition on ordinary legislative appropriations.
Do not claim every restriction on citizen initiatives applies identically to the Legislature unless another supplied provision expressly says so.
Do not omit the §13.1(7) three-year bar on reinitiating a failed initiative on the same or substantially similar grounds if discussing graceful degradation or repeat use.

title: Remainder viability convention fallback and cooldown
must: Recognize that competing petitions within 90 days or a finding that the remainder could not realistically satisfy Statehood Audit conditions sends the affected matters to a Territory Convention.
Recognize that the Convention has 90 days from its first session to produce a proposed resolution.

Recognize that if no resolution is produced, all petitions addressed there lapse together, the Territory continues undivided, and substantially the same geographic petitions face a three-year reinitiation bar.
Recognize that any Convention resolution must be ratified by the affected eligible voters and then proceeds through the otherwise applicable §15.2 or §15.4 process.
mustNot: Do not claim ordinary §15.2 lapse and reinitiation automatically overrides the three-year cooldown created by this provision.
Do not claim the JMC itself chooses the final boundary or constitutional status.
Do not invent substantive terms the Territory Convention must adopt; the provision sets none.
